content: Stripe Checkout's success-page redirect and the webhook delivery are two independent, unordered signals -- the browser can land on /success before the webhook has been processed, or the webhook can complete first. Naive integrations that grant access only on the redirect (trusting a client-supplied session_id with no server verification) create both a false-positive window (webhook still catching up) and a spoofable gap (anyone can hit /success?session_id=fake). Correct pattern: the success-page handler should server-side re-fetch the Checkout Session / Subscription from Stripe's API (not trust the URL param blindly) to reconcile immediately, while the webhook remains the authoritative, idempotent source of truth that runs independently in the background -- both paths converge on the same atomic state-transition logic so whichever arrives first does the update and the other is a safe no-op.
